title: Unbounded string copy with stpcpy ({lang})
description: The code copies with {sink}, which writes until the source terminator and returns a pointer to the end. There is no destination size, so a source longer than the buffer overwrites whatever follows it.
remediation: Copy with an explicit bound, for example {safe}, and check that the result fits before writing.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the copy without tracking the destination size.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on unbounded string copies in {lang} code.
fp: A copy into a buffer that provably exceeds the longest constant source is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} has no destination limit. Any source that is not a compile-time constant decides how much memory is written.
applicability: Path and message assembly in C code.
risk: Stack or heap corruption from attacker-sized input; HIGH severity.
why: {lang} has no destination bound in the copy ({sink}).
fix: Use a bounded copy and check the result ({safe}).
Keep the destination size beside the buffer.
verifyT: Rescan shows no unbounded string copy.

title: Unbounded wide-string concatenation ({lang})
description: The code appends a wide string with {sink}, which has no destination size and counts nothing. Repeated appends in a loop grow past the allocation without any single call looking wrong.
remediation: Append with a bounded helper that takes the remaining element count, for example {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the append without tracking buffer growth across iterations.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on wide-string concatenation in {lang} code.
fp: An append into a fixed buffer that is reset on every iteration is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} appends until the source terminator. A loop over attacker-controlled items therefore writes past the end at the item where the buffer fills.
applicability: Wide-string message building in Windows-oriented C code.
risk: Heap corruption in a loop that is easy to trigger remotely; HIGH severity.
why: {lang} has no destination bound in the append ({sink}).
fix: Use a bounded append with the remaining capacity ({safe}).
Reset or reallocate the buffer per iteration.
verifyT: Rescan shows no unbounded wide-string append.

title: Windows API string copy without a limit ({lang})
description: The code copies a string with {sink}, the Windows API copy that has no destination size. The destination is always a fixed buffer in practice, so a longer source overwrites adjacent memory.
remediation: Use the counted variant with an explicit destination size, for example {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the copy without checking the destination size.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on Windows API string copies in {lang} code.
fp: Copies from a constant into a buffer larger than the constant are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} copies until the source terminator. Registry values and command-line arguments are the usual sources that exceed the buffer.
applicability: Windows services, installers and registry handling in C.
risk: Stack corruption from registry or command-line data; HIGH severity.
why: {lang} has no destination size in the API ({sink}).
verifyT: Rescan shows no unbounded Windows API copy.

title: Reflective member access in application code ({lang})
description: The code reaches a member through {sink}. Reflection selects the method or field by name at runtime, so a name that comes from a request runs a member the developer never intended to expose.
remediation: Keep reflective lookups on constant names, and gate any dynamic lookup behind an allowlist, for example {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the reflective call without tracing the name.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on reflective member access in {lang} code.
fp: Framework and test code that reflects on a constant class name is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} resolves a member by string. Frameworks use this deliberately; application code that copies a request parameter into the name hands the caller the member selection.
applicability: Serializers, mappers and plugin loaders in Java.
risk: Invocation of unintended methods, including setters that change security state; MEDIUM severity.
why: {lang} selects the member by name at runtime ({sink}).
fix: Use constant names and an allowlist ({safe}).
verifyT: Rescan shows reflective lookups restricted to constant names.

java:reflect: an interface call on a typed object

title: Encoded payload decoded in application code ({lang})
description: PHP code decodes a value with {sink}. Decoding is how packed payloads are hidden from string review, and when the result reaches an include or an eval it becomes code the reviewer never saw.
remediation: Decode only in a reviewed location, validate the decoded content against a schema, and never pass the result to an interpreter, for example {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the decode without following the value.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on payload decoding in {lang} code.
fp: Decoding a signed token or an image attachment is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} turns opaque text into content. In a codebase with any include or eval path, the decoded value is the shortest route from a request to execution.
applicability: Upload handlers, plugin loaders and legacy modules in PHP.
risk: Concealed code execution when the decoded value reaches an interpreter; MEDIUM severity.
why: {lang} decoding hides the payload from review ({sink}).
fix: Validate decoded content and keep it away from the interpreter ({safe}).
Prefer structured formats with explicit parsing.
verifyT: Rescan shows decoded values never reaching include or eval.

php:decode: a structured decode with schema validation

title: Compressed input expanded without a size limit ({lang})
description: The code expands compressed data with {sink}. A few kilobytes of crafted input expand to gigabytes, and the expansion happens before any check can run, so the worker dies with the request in flight.
remediation: Bound the output size or stream the expansion with a byte budget, for example {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the expansion without knowing the output size.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on decompression in {lang} code.
fp: Expanding an archive the service itself produced, with a known small size, is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} allocates according to the compressed stream's own claims. Nothing in the call compares that claim with the memory available.
applicability: Upload handlers, backup importers and API endpoints that accept compressed bodies.
risk: Denial of service from a small request; MEDIUM severity.
why: {lang} trusts the expansion ratio in the stream ({sink}).
fix: Cap the output at a documented maximum ({safe}).
Reject streams whose declared size exceeds the cap before expanding.
verifyT: Rescan shows a size cap on every expansion path.

php:zlib: a streamed expansion with a byte budget

title: Native library loaded by name ({lang})
description: The code loads a native library through {sink}. The name is resolved by the platform loader, which searches the working directory and the library path before trusted locations, so a planted file is loaded instead of the packaged one.
remediation: Load a packaged library by absolute path, or verify its signature before loading, for example {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the load without resolving the name.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on native library loads in {lang} code.
fp: Loads of a bundled library from a read-only directory are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} asks the platform to find a library by name. Any directory earlier in the search order can answer with a different file.
applicability: JNI wrappers, desktop applications and services that load optional native code.
risk: Arbitrary native code execution in the process; HIGH severity.
why: {lang} resolves the library name through the platform search order ({sink}).
fix: Load from an absolute packaged path ({safe}).
Keep the working directory non-writable and verify the library hash.
verifyT: Rescan shows every native load using a resolved, verified path.

java:jni: an absolute path with a verified hash
